title: Ephemeral affinity bounce causing intermittent batch drought
creator: Ethan Morales
description: Summary: During a low-traffic window on 2026-03-04 we observed repeated, short-lived periods where the continuous batching layer stopped forming useful coalesced batches for ~120-450ms intervals ("batch droughts"), leading to transient 95/99th token latency spikes and unfair request ordering across priority tiers. Multiple customer-facing routes experienced increased latency and a small number of requests hit the high-latency fallback path. This ticket tracks the post-incident follow-ups, root cause analysis, and action items.

impact: User-facing: transient increases in token generation latency for ~0.2% of requests across multiple customers; one partner integration reported degraded perceived responsiveness for 18 minutes. Internal: SLO churn for token P95 increased, triggered paging. No data loss or correctness regressions observed.
root_cause: A recent change to the rate-limit recentering algorithm (token_bucket recenter frequency adjustment) introduced slight, periodic bursts of request reclassification. At the same time, a regression in our affinity TTL handling caused ephemeral affinity IDs to flip frequently between scheduling cohorts ("affinity bounce"). The combination caused many short-lived requests to miss aggregation into existing active batches and instead be scheduled into tiny single-request microbatches or bypass batching entirely, producing the observed batch drought and tail latency spikes. Secondary contributor: aggressive KV cache eviction thresholds removed warm prefix entries earlier-than-expected, preventing reuse across the affinity flips.
mitigation_taken: Rolled back the recentering change to previous stable parameters, patched affinity TTL handling to respect minimum adhesion window, and temporarily relaxed KV cache eviction thresholds. Deployed mitigations as a hotfix to runtime-1.24 on 2026-03-04 04:05 UTC. Post-deploy monitoring showed P95 latencies returned to baseline within 8 minutes.
short_term_actions: Backport affinity TTL fix to all active runtime branches (owner: Lina Chen, due: 2026-03-14)
Pin rate-limit recentering parameters until we can run systematic replays (owner: Marco Rivera, due: 2026-03-12 - Completed)
Increase KV cache warm retention by 25% for cohorts that saw >5% affinity churn (owner: Priya Singh, due: 2026-03-15)
Add temporary alerting for batch-formation delta > 200ms over 1m window (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-13)
Run traffic replay of last 72 hours with instrumentation turned on to validate fix (owner: Ethan Morales, due: 2026-03-16)
long_term_actions: Introduce affinity stickiness telemetry and 30-day dashboards to measure churn by deployment and model (owner: Observability, due: 2026-04-15)
Design a bounded reclassification policy for rate-limit recentering that respects active batch membership (owner: Scheduling team, due: 2026-05-01)
Implement KV cache adaptive eviction tuned by observed affinity churn to avoid premature prefix eviction (owner: Runtime team, due: 2026-05-01)
Add deterministic batching replay harness into CI to catch micro-drought regressions before canary (owner: Test infra, due: 2026-04-01)
Run an incident simulation exercise focused on low-traffic windows and affinity flapping scenarios (owner: EngOps, due: 2026-06-01)
